datasets.title: تقييم الأضرار في جنديرس، منطقة عفرين، محافظة حلب في 11 فبراير Syrian Arab Republic: 2023
datasets.description: UNOSAT code EQ20230206SYR, GDACS Id: 1357372 توضح هذه الخريطة المباني التي يحتمل أنها تتضررت من جراء زلزال 06 فبراير 2023 في جنديرس في منطقة عفرين (محافظة حلب)، كما تم اكتشافها من صورة القمر الصناعي عالية الدقة Pleiades التي تم الحصول عليها في 11 فبراير 2023. في مدينة جنديرس، حدد يونوسات 228 مبنى متضررا و318 مبنى يحتمل أن يكون متضررا. هذا تحليل أولي ولم يتم التحقق من صحته بعد على الأرض. يرجى إرسال التعليقات الأرضية إلى مركز الأمم المتحدة للأقمار الصناعية (يونوسات). [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/tqyym-ldrr-fy-jndyrs-mntq-fryn-mhfz-hlb-fy-11-fbryr-2023]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts compared high-resolution Pleiades satellite imagery acquired on 11 February 2023 with pre-event baseline imagery to identify building damage caused by the 6 February 2023 earthquake in Jindiris. Buildings were classified into damage categories (confirmed damaged, likely damaged) through visual interpretation of structural changes visible in the satellite data.

sources.name: United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Post-event satellite imagery analysis using Pleiades high-resolution imagery acquired on 11 February 2023 to detect and classify building damage from the 6 February 2023 earthquake
